title: This Animal Smells Exactly Like Buttered Popcorn. Now We Know Why
subject: binturong

scenes.text: An animal in Asia smells exactly like buttered popcorn. Nobody cooked it.
It's the binturong, a tree-climbing bearcat. Walk near one and your nose says movie theater.
In 2016, scientists tested 33 of them. Every single one had the same chemical in its urine.
It's the molecule that gives popcorn its smell. Popcorn makes it by popping, with heat.
A binturong can't pop anything. Scientists think bacteria on its skin and fur make it.
Males carry more, and they drag it through the trees. Buttered popcorn means: someone lives here.

description:
A binturong smells like buttered popcorn, and in 2016 scientists found out why.
They tested 33 binturongs and found the same popcorn molecule, 2-AP, in every one. Popcorn makes it with heat, but a binturong can't cook, so researchers think bacteria make it. Binturongs use the scent to mark territory and find mates.
Would you follow your nose to a binturong?
first_comment: Would you rather meet a binturong or smell a popcorn machine? Fun bonus: their prehensile tail works like a fifth hand.
